Finance & banking

The start, and the pivot

I studied finance and spent my first working years as a personal banker. It was stable and it wasn’t for me. I kept finding the problem-solving more interesting than the paperwork, and I kept coming back to design. Eventually I committed to the switch and never looked back.

FinanceBankingThe pivot

How I work 04

Opinionated on purpose. Adjusted every time.

01

Interrogate the brief

Before screens: what does the business actually need, what can engineering actually ship, and what are people doing today instead?

02

Make the flow visible

Journey maps and flows before pixels. Most problems are structural, and structural problems are cheaper to find on a whiteboard.

03

Design the system, not the screen

Components, states, edge cases, tokens. If it only works on the happy path, it does not work.

04

Stay until it ships

Handoff, build review, design QA. The version that ships is the only version that counts.

Background

The part that isn't on the résumé.

I like the whole problem, not just the visible part of it. Most of my work has been in small teams where the designer owns it end to end, the research, the wires, the screens, the prototype, and the awkward QA pass three days before release.

I'm Monalisha, a self-taught product designer currently residing in Bengaluru. I try to understand the business before I touch the interface, and I care more about whether something works than whether it photographs well.

Outside work I'm usually travelling, taking photos, cooking, or with my people and my pets.
